sampling_model.design: Observational sampling from a fixed population law; identification is the primary target.
sampling_model.units: Independent draws \((X_i,A_i,Y_i)\sim P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) with finite \(\mathcal X\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment may depend on \((X,U)\); the candidate full-data law restores conditional ignorability given \((X,U)\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed stratum has \(0<p_x<1\); constant-\(U\) boundary laws are retained in the closure, and latent positivity is allowed to vanish only in the all-budget Manski limit.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Use a nonredundant empirical-frequency or asymptotically linear estimator of \((\lambda_x,p_x,r_{0,x},r_{1,x})_{x\in\mathcal X}\).  On a unique nondegenerate active branch, implicit differentiation of the certified equations gives the pointwise Gaussian endpoint and normal-frontier limits.  Uniform inference through optimizer ties, legal-root collisions, stationary continua, and higher-order algebraic contacts remains open.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For fixed sensitivity parameters, the binary mixtures have unique maximum-likelihood solutions and yield a recalculated average treatment effect.
Quantile balancing gives the sharp ATE interval under the marginal sensitivity model.

For binary or low-level categorical exposure and binary outcome, an exposure-standardization sensitivity function is variation-independent of the observed-data distribution and supports three consistent estimators of marginal causal effects.
General bias formulas specialize to outcome contrasts multiplied by changes in the distribution of a binary confounder.
A sharp joint relative-risk bounding factor applies to an unrestricted unmeasured confounder.
A breakdown frontier is the boundary between assumptions that do and do not support a chosen conclusion.
With no restriction on treatment selection, binary potential-outcome means obey worst-case treatment-response bounds.

body.tldr: For binary treatment and outcome, one shared latent binary confounder, and finite categorical \(X\), the paper derives the exact ATE interval over its own closed common-confounder odds-budget class.  Binary-logistic formulas provide coordinates for the strictly positive chart, but the class is not attributed wholesale to Rosenbaum--Rubin.  A unique quadratic-mixture root reduces each outcome budget to two analytic branches, and both arms optimize over the same posterior pair.  Constructive closure laws prove sharpness; exact fixed-input and parametric semialgebraic procedures certify endpoints and the zero-tipping surface.  A complete deterministic rational artifact certifies strict tightening over the internal separate-pair relaxation.  On a unique nondegenerate active branch, the estimated tipping frontier has an explicit root-\(n\) normal-displacement law with standard-error constant \(\sigma_L/\|\nabla_\gamma L\|\); uniform Hausdorff inference at ties, root collisions, stationary continua, and higher-order contacts remains open.

project_justification.gap: Rosenbaum and Rubin analyze a binary-\(U\), binary-response logistic sensitivity calculation at fixed parameter tuples.  The cited sections do not state this paper's union over arm-specific two-sided outcome-odds budgets, unrestricted coupling of the two potential outcomes, finite-simplex closure, or optimization over one common posterior pair.  Contemporary propensity-only, arbitrary-confounder, and exposure-standardized models likewise do not provide this common-pair envelope.  Existing directional methods do not by themselves give uniformly honest Hausdorff inference when the certified algebraic active set changes dimension or contact order.
project_justification.niche: The maintained class is low dimensional and scientifically calibratable while preserving cross-arm compatibility that separate armwise relaxations discard.  Its semialgebraic geometry supports exact population endpoints, a reproducible strict-gap witness, a multibudget tipping frontier, and an explicit regular-branch sampling law.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the sharp interval for its stated common-binary-confounder class, records only a binary-logistic coordinate equivalence and fixed-tuple recovery relative to Rosenbaum--Rubin, supplies exact fixed-input and parametric algebraic procedures, and certifies strict internal-relaxation tightening with a complete deterministic artifact and continuity of optimized values.  It also proves pointwise regular tipping inference and isolates uniform singular-frontier inference as a precise open problem.

body.related_work: Rosenbaum and Rubin \cite{RosenbaumRubin1983Sensitivity} study binary \(U\) and binary response through fixed treatment and response logistic sensitivity parameters and recalculate adjusted response rates at a fixed tuple.  This paper uses that fixed-tuple algebraic coordinate calculation only; it does not call its bounded arm-specific odds-budget union, unrestricted potential-outcome coupling, or finite-simplex closure the published Rosenbaum--Rubin class.  VanderWeele and Arah \cite{VanderWeeleArah2011Bias} provide the bias-decomposition identity motivating the arm-mean map.  Ciocănea-Teodorescu, Gabriel, and Sjölander \cite{CiocaneaGabrielSjolander2022Marginal} use variation-independent exposure-standardization sensitivity parameters, while Ding and VanderWeele \cite{DingVanderWeele2016WithoutAssumptions} derive an arbitrary-\(U\) relative-risk factor.  Tan \cite{Tan2006MarginalSensitivity}, Yadlowsky et al. \cite{YadlowskyEtAl2022Bounds}, and Dorn and Guo \cite{DornGuo2023QuantileBalancing} restrict latent treatment odds without this simultaneous common-binary treatment-and-outcome odds geometry.  These published models are generally non-nested with the present class, so the strict comparison in this paper is only with its internal separate-posterior-pair relaxation.  Masten and Poirier \cite{MastenPoirier2020BreakdownFrontier} motivate assumption-frontier inference; Fang and Santos \cite{FangSantos2019InferenceDirectional} provide generic pointwise directional theory; and Nabi et al. \cite{NabiEtAl2024SemiparametricSensitivity} develop adjacent smooth sensitivity inference.  The regular active branch here reduces to an ordinary Gaussian normal-displacement law, whereas uniform Hausdorff inference for moving algebraic ties, collisions, continua, and order-\(k\) contacts is not supplied by those results.  Manski \cite{Manski1990TreatmentResponse} is recovered only in the joint infinite-budget limit with vanishing latent positivity.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The sharp population envelope and the general fixed-input and parametric semialgebraic procedures are separate from the worked rational witness.  The strict-gap claim relies on a deterministic exact artifact that must expose the complete stationary polynomials, Sturm chains or equivalent isolators, legal-cell inventory, denominator saturations, and objective enclosure for every competitor; neighborhood strictness then follows from continuity of compact optimized values, not from unverified persistence of one named branch.  The inference theorem is pointwise and assumes strictly positive observed cells, finite interior budgets, one unique analytic active branch, an invertible stationary Jacobian, nonzero denominators, strict inactive inequalities and objective separation, an asymptotically linear observed-summary estimator, and \(\nabla_\gamma L\neq0\).  It does not establish uniform coverage at ties, legal-root collisions, stationary continua, or order-\(k\) contacts, where the sharp Hausdorff rate and leading law remain open.
body.honest_scope: The population target is the ATE identified set for the paper's explicitly defined common-binary-confounder class, not for every model historically called a Rosenbaum--Rubin sensitivity model.  The historical citation supports only the binary-logistic fixed-tuple recalculation used as a coordinate check; it does not establish the paper's bounded union, arbitrary coupling, closure, or sharp envelope.  Endpoint attainment is over the closed finite-simplex class; over the strictly positive chart only infima, suprema, and closure are asserted unless an optimizer is interior.  The separate-pair interval is an internal outer relaxation, and strict tightening is asserted only through the complete exact witness artifact and continuity of the optimized values.  Sampling inference is proved pointwise on a unique nondegenerate active branch, with normal-displacement constant \(\sigma_L/\|\nabla_\gamma L\|\).  Uniformly honest frontier inference at optimizer ties, root collisions, positive-dimensional stationary sets, and higher-order algebraic contacts is an explicit open question.  The model retains one binary confounder, finite categorical \(X\), and observed overlap; Manski recovery occurs only as all odds budgets diverge while latent positivity may vanish.
